projects.title: Desk Research
projects.description:
These sources mainly focus on the materials, manufacturing, lifespan, repair, and disposal of headphones. Research shows that most of a headphone’s climate impact comes from the manufacturing process, while replacing batteries or parts and extending its lifespan can reduce environmental impact. Other examples also show that repairable design can be more important than simply using “green” materials. For example, some headphones can be charged by solar energy but are still difficult to repair or recycle. I plan to show the process of headphones being used, breaking, taken apart, and repaired to connect these ideas into one story.

1.The Climate Impact of the Usage of Headphones and Headsets
2.Useful metals recovery from electronic scraps of headphones – A sustainable approach
3.From Waste to Worth: The Case for Modular and Upgradable Electronics in a Sustainable Future.
4.Reparability Scoring System – Product relevance scoping study (2025)
5.Fairbuds XL review: the excellent noise-cancelling headphones you can fix yourself
6.Sony 1000XX the Collexion headphones review: supreme comfort and quiet luxury for your ears
7.Urbanista Los Angeles review: solar charging headphones for epic battery
8.Golden business opportunity hidden in consumer goods

projects.title: Troubleshooting my blog website
projects.description:
This week, I worked on a problem with my blog website. Although I had already written my blog, the content was not appearing on the website. At first, I followed the instructions provided by teacher, but I encountered some errors. Since I did not understand what went wrong, I decided to ask GPT for help.

During this process, I learned more about Git, GitHub, and GitHub Pages. Git is a tool for tracking changes in files, while GitHub is used to store and manage projects online. GitHub Pages can publish a website from a GitHub repository. I also used AI to help me understand error messages and troubleshoot the problems.

First, I followed the teacher’s instructions and entered Git commands in the terminal. However, several warnings appeared, and I was unsure what to do next. I took screenshots and asked GPT to explain the errors. Then, I followed its suggestions, checked my Git status, looked through the GitHub Actions error logs, and tried to fix the problem step by step.

1.When I first tried to upload my changes, the terminal showed a warning about an embedded Git repository. At that time, I did not understand what it meant, so I sent a screenshot to GPT.GPT explained that I had added Git repositories inside another Git repository. It suggested removing the nested repositories from Git's tracking.However, when I first tried the suggested command, another error appeared. I realised that fixing a coding problem was not always as simple as following one instruction.
2.I then checked GitHub Actions and found that my website deployment had failed.At first, I only knew that the build had failed, but I did not understand why. After opening the error logs, I found a message saying that GitHub could not find the URL for a submodule.I showed this error to GPT, which helped me understand that the nested Git repositories were affecting the deployment process.
3.Following AI's suggestions, I used Git commands to remove the nested repository entries from the main repository's tracking. I also edited the .gitignore file to prevent the same problem from happening again.During this process, I learned the purpose of several Git commands, including git status, git add, git commit, and git push.After making these changes, I committed them with the message "Fix nested repositories" and successfully pushed the changes to GitHub.

The most challenging part was that I did not understand the error messages or the commands at first. Sometimes, following AI's suggestions led to new errors, so I needed to keep asking questions and checking the results.This experience helped me understand that AI can be useful for solving coding problems, but it is also important to understand what each command does instead of simply copying it.

projects.title: crit project 0
projects.description:
We learned how to conduct a project crit using a four-step process. We also had the opportunity to discuss our projects with others. This experience helped me understand that a crit is not simply about judging whether a project is good or bad, but about understanding and developing ideas through discussion.
Before this session, I thought a crit was mainly about receiving suggestions from teachers or classmates. However, I realised that it is also about learning how to ask useful questions and understand someone else's creative decisions.
During the discussion, I found that different people could interpret the same project in different ways. Sometimes, questions from others could reveal something that the creator had not considered before.
I also learned that giving feedback is not always about finding problems or suggesting solutions. Asking questions can encourage the creator to reflect on their own work.
I think this approach is useful because it creates space for discussion rather than simply telling someone what they should change.
